name: How long the cooperative tin lasts
subject: accounting
brief: The Class XI commerce cooperative keeps a locked tin for geometry-box and graph-pad vouchers. On Monday morning the tin holds 2,400 rupees. Counter sales bring in 350 rupees a day and supplier vouchers take out 650 rupees a day. The cooperative's rule is that the tin must never drop below 900 rupees. A group has worked out that the tin can run for 8 days before it reaches that float. You are the critic, and there is only the daybook's one pair of readings to test it against.

quantities.name: Rupees held in the petty-cash tin
Rupees paid in at the counter a day
Rupees paid out on supplier vouchers a day
Working days until the tin reaches the 900-rupee float
Shop price of one graph pad

note: Set in the commerce classroom at Nabapara Vidyalaya (loc_nhss). Worked answer: the tin loses 650 - 350 = 300 rupees a day, and it may fall from 2,400 to the 900-rupee float, a drop of 1,500 rupees, which takes 1,500 / 300 = 5 working days. The group's 8 days is the plausible mistake: 2,400 / 300 = 8 forgets that the float must stay in the tin. There is no fault in the figures.
